newsitem.title: USA: WPS Resources says Q4, year earnings hurt.
newsitem.headline: WPS Resources says Q4, year earnings hurt.

text.p: WPS Resources Corp said Monday its earnings for the fourth quarter and full year will be hurt by several factors, including an increase of up to $3.5 million in purchased power expenses at Wisconsin Public Service Corp.
That increase was due to an extended shutdown of the Kewaunee Nuclear Power Plant and an increase in maintenance expense of about $1.4 million due to the repair of the Kewaunee steam generators.
It also cited a loss of about $2,00,000 at its WPS Energy Serivces Inc gas marketing unit due to volatile gas prices.

WPS said its earnings will also be hurt by a writeoff of about $2 million from an investment at WPS Power Development Inc, a non-regulated subsidiary, and additional electric repair expenses of about $1 million at Wisconsin Public Service due to a severe ice storm.
All the expenses are before income taxes and were not reflected in earnings as of September 30, the company said.

Wisconsin Public Service operates and has a 41.2 percent ownership interest in Kewaunee. As previously reported, Kewaunee was taken out of service on September 21 for scheduled refueling and maintenance.

The outage was expected to last five weeks, but inspection of previously repaired steam generator tubes showed continued degradation of the repair joints. This prevents further operation of the Kewaunee plant until the tubes are repaired or the two steam generators are replaced, the company said.
Kewaunee is expected to be returned to service with repaired steam generators in the first quarter of 1997, but the company cautioned that the timing of repairs cannot be forecast with any precision.
The utility said Wisconsin Public Service's share of the total cost of repairing the corroded tubes would increase expenses by as much as $2.27 million, including the $1.4 million indicated for 1996.

For the remainder of 1996, Wisconsin Public Service has essentially no financial protection for the additional purchased power costs associated with an extended outage, it added. For 1997, Wisconsin Public Service is pursuing regulatory approval for one of several ways to recover its costs.
Wisconsin Public Service said it will have sufficient capacity to supply electricity to customers during the Kewaunee outage.
